title: Design System: Arova — The Graphite Edition

void.note: The permanent icon rail — the darkest thing on screen. Part of the six-step graphite ramp.

sunken.note: Inputs, tab track, meters, code wells — deliberately darker than the working ground.

panel.note: The section panel and the activity board ground.

sheet.note: The body/work-surface ground a thread or pane sits on.

card.note: Raised content: bars, cards, rows, thread entries, dialog fill.

raised.note: Hover / selected / tab track / floating toast+jump. The lightest resting surface; ink-3 clears 4.5:1 on it.

ink.note: Primary text on every graphite surface.

ink-3.note: Tertiary/metadata, timestamps, placeholders. Tuned to clear 4.5:1 on --raised.

rule-2.note: Stronger border: icon buttons, ghost, inputs, chips, dashed provisional edges, idle dots.

azure.note: The ONE interaction colour: active nav, focus ring, links, caret, primary fill, meters, list markers. Its dark glyph is --on-azure.

azure-bright.note: Hover on an azure surface; active rail label.

azure-wash.note: Azure dark-ground tint: selected rail button, focus glow ring, .row-focus, .chip.azure.

azure-line.note: Azure tint border for .chip.azure. Same literal is reused as ::selection.

on-azure.note: The dark glyph every azure fill takes. A light accent on a dark ground cannot carry white text.

ran.note: RESERVED: a stored row recorded a completed/approved action. Never on an interactive affordance.

ran-wash.note: Dark-ground tint; the pulse.on glow ring; .chip.ran fill.

waiting.note: RESERVED: queued/running/pending/due. Real pending only. Rail badge ink is #17140d.

fault.note: RESERVED: failed/cancelled/rejected/provider error. The .danger ghost ink and delete mark fill.

fault-wash.note: Fault entry panel and danger-ghost hover fill.

fault-line.note: .chip.fault border and the fault entry panel.

code-bg.note: The only recessed dark surface other than the rail — fenced model output reads deliberately darker than everything.

code-line.note: Frame + bar divider inside the code block.

hue-sage.note: identity.ts tint: ink/tile #a8d98a · glyph #2c372a · wash #353d36 · line #4c5c47. Answers 'which agent', never status. One of exactly three.

hue-aqua.note: identity.ts tint: ink/tile #70d2db · glyph #21363a · wash #2e3c41 · line #3b5a5f.

hue-mauve.note: identity.ts tint: ink/tile #c4a3dd · glyph #322d3b · wash #393641 · line #544c60.

identityRationale.note: identity.ts exports exactly three tints. This is a measured limit, not taste: with one azure owning interaction and green/amber/red owning state, the cool half of the wheel has room for three marks at 30 degrees of separation, so identity is led by the avatar glyph and the tint is secondary.
tests: every tint ink clears 4.5:1 on sheet, card, raised, panel
every tint glyph clears 4.5:1 on its tile, and no tile is ever given a white glyph (ratio to #fff stays below 3)
each tint sits >=30 degrees from the accent and from every state colour
the three tints are >=30 degrees apart from each other
no tint collides with a state colour and none reads warm
assignment (FNV-1a) is deterministic and exercises the whole palette; a missing key falls back to HUES[0], never a crash
identityRationale.addingAFourth: Requires changing the accent or the state semantics first — the separation and no-warm-drift tests fail otherwise.

display.purpose: Manrope 700–800, -.022em, lh 1.2. h1 26px base; 22px identity bar, 20px sheet bar, 24px pane head, 26px/800 editable org name.

body.purpose: DM Sans 400 14px/1.6 — chrome, labels, list rows, everything not a heading, label or measurement.

reading.purpose: Thread replies and composer at 15px/1.7, hard 80ch measure (--measure). RichText re-typesets model markdown into React nodes (never HTML); list markers take --h-ink.

label.purpose: Uppercase 700 ~11px tracking .08em: group labels, pane-h2, chips, entry tags, field labels. The only uppercase device and never a kicker above a heading.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono tabular-nums, -.01em, 9.5–12.5px. Measurement ONLY: stamps, counts, char/token figures, model ids, code, fault detail. Never prose.

fontLoading.name: self-hosted-next-font
fontLoading.value: DM_Sans -> --font-body, Manrope -> --font-display, JetBrains_Mono -> --font-mono (next/font, display swap, applied in layout.tsx)
fontLoading.purpose: No remote @import; the family names inside CSS font stacks are fallbacks only.

shadows.name: shadow-lift
shadows.purpose: The ONLY shadow token. Floating layers only: .dialog, .toast, .jump, and the two overlay drawers (.board at <=1250, .sidepanel at <=860). Resting surfaces, cards, rows and inputs have no shadow.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single system ease (var(--ease)); every timed transition uses it.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: The one entrance settle: dialog .26s, toast .22s, jump pill .20s.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: The only loop: the 2px --h-ink streaming caret AND the In-flight row's caret-st dot are literally the same @keyframes blink. Reduced-motion: rests at opacity .6.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button hover/active 120ms background-and-press transitions; primary translateY(1px), send adds scale(.97), rail-logo scale(1.05).

motion.name: surface-shift
motion.purpose: Composer box border/background/shadow shift; rail/agent-card hover ground change; entry-tools opacity reveal.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) clamps all animation/transition durations to .01ms with one iteration; .caret, .caret-st rest at opacity .6
motion.purpose: Global clamp shipped; new motion must fall inside it.

breakpoints.name: board-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: The activity board leaves the grid and becomes a right-side overlay drawer (min(372px,92vw), shadow-lift); .only-narrow affordances appear.

breakpoints.name: panel-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: The section panel becomes a full-width step overlay (mpanel); --rail-w narrows to 60px, --gutter to 18px; sheet-bar compresses; .only-mobile appears, .only-wide hides.

breakpoints.name: grid-2up
breakpoints.purpose: Agent grid and org stats drop to two columns; create button collapses to a bare icon; section-aside hides.

layoutDimensions.name: rail-w
layoutDimensions.purpose: var(--rail-w): the permanent icon rail (60px at <=860).

layoutDimensions.name: workbench
layoutDimensions.purpose: The four-column grid at wide; the panel can collapse to 0.

layoutDimensions.name: measure
layoutDimensions.purpose: var(--measure): the prose/thread cap for entry text, prov line, consult and rich blocks.

layoutDimensions.name: gutter
layoutDimensions.purpose: var(--gutter): thread and composer horizontal rhythm (thread left padding is gutter+6); tightens to 18px at <=860.

layoutDimensions.name: thread-column
layoutDimensions.purpose: Max width of the thread; panes cap at 1020px.

layoutDimensions.name: depth-step
layoutDimensions.purpose: Per-level indent of seat nodes via --depth; org-chart rows indent 15px.

browserSurface.name: selection
browserSurface.purpose: Azure-tint highlight (reuses the azure-line literal). One-off, not a token.

browserSurface.name: caret
browserSurface.purpose: Azure text cursor in every field.

browserSurface.name: scrollbar
browserSurface.value: ::-webkit-scrollbar 11px; thumb #3b4149 with 3px sheet outline, radius 9px; hover #4b525c; transparent track
browserSurface.purpose: Sheet-outlined channel. The thumb greys and the 9px radius are one-offs.

browserSurface.name: focus-ring
browserSurface.value: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--azure); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); }
browserSurface.purpose: The one system focus treatment: a 2px azure outline at 2px offset. Never suppressed.

oneOffLiterals.note: Single-use hexes kept deliberately OUTSIDE :root so the design detector does not read them as drift. Rule: a second use promotes them to :root.
hoverSteps: #1f2226 section item / node / board row hover

components.description: The one action on a surface. Azure fill, dark on-azure glyph, 6px radius, presses 1px at 120ms. Flat at rest — no shadow.

components.name: Ghost & Danger Buttons
components.description: Default secondary: sheet ground, firm rule-2 border, ink text; hover lifts the border to #575f6a and the ground to raised. Danger stays a GHOST recoloured to fault ink + fault-line border, hover fills fault-wash — never a filled red button.

components.name: Send Button
components.description: 34px square filled with the selected agent's identity tile (--h-tile, azure by default) with a DARK glyph — never white. Brightness hover, scale press.
components.html: <button class="ds-send" aria-label="Send message"><svg width="17" height="17" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M5 12h14"/><path d="m12 5 7 7-7 7"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-send { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 34px; height: 34px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 6px); background: var(--h-tile, var(--azure, #7ba6ef)); color: var(--h-glyph, var(--on-azure, #0e1a2b)); cursor: pointer; transition: transform .12s var(--ease, cubic-bezier(.22,.68,.31,1)), filter .12s; } .ds-send:hover { filter: brightness(1.12); } .ds-send:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(.97); } .ds-send:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--azure, #7ba6ef); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-send:disabled { opacity: .45; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Icon Rail Button
components.description: The permanent void rail. Buttons are ink-3 at rest, lift to #1e2126+ink on hover, and read active as azure-wash + azure-bright with a 3px azure tab bleeding off the edge. Logo tile is azure with a dark glyph. Count badge is amber.

components.name: Seat Node
components.description: The signature bench row: a glyph-first identity tile (dark glyph on the tint), a stored-state dot, name, mono count + relative time, role beneath. Selected fills --h-wash and inverts the tile to --h-tile/--h-glyph. Indents 14px per reporting depth. The wrapper carries the agent's --h-* inline; a missing key never crashes.

components.name: State Chip
components.description: Uppercase pill with a leading dot of currentColor. ran/waiting/fault each take the matching state wash + state ink + state line; idle is raised + ink-2 (samples and unconfigured); azure is the interaction tint. State chips only ever render from toneOf(status) on a stored row.

components.name: Field / Text Input
components.description: Uppercase label over a sunken well with a firm rule-2 border, 6px radius. Focus shifts the border to azure and rings a 3px azure-wash glow (the composer swaps azure for the active identity hue). Placeholder is ink-3, which clears 4.5:1 on raised.
components.html: Edit and press Enter or click away to save.

components.name: Agent Card
components.description: A 216px min card on the Overview grid: card ground + rule hairline, 38px identity avatar tile (glyph-first), name, role, then a live dot in ran (or ink-3 when paused) with a mono message count. Hover shifts the border to the tint's line and the ground to #282b30. Flat at rest — no shadow.

narrative.overview:
Arova is not a dashboard wearing a dark theme; it is an instrument bench. A permanent icon rail owns navigation at the far left, a contextual section panel owns the list you are working through beside it, the fluid work surface carries the single title of whatever you opened, and the activity board on the right is a printer that only emits rows the server actually stored. The whole world is graphite: neutral surfaces step toward the reader, ink stays neutral, and colour is rationed to three jobs — azure for interaction, green/amber/red for a stored state, and a fixed set of identity tints for which agent you are looking at. Nothing implies work that did not happen.

Density is the aesthetic. This is a working tool read every day by one operator who wants to continue, not tour. So the surfaces are dark and close together, hairlines and surface steps do the structural work that shadows would do elsewhere, and there is no hero, no decorative illustration, no repeated heading. The identity tints are led by the avatar glyph, not the hue — the hue is a secondary marker precisely because there are only three and they cannot carry the whole identity load.
keyCharacteristics: Six graphite surfaces (void to sunken) that step toward the reader; elevation is carried by surface steps and hairlines, not shadows.
One cool azure does all interactive work; its dark-ground tint family (wash/line) and a dark glyph live alongside it.
Green/amber/red exist only where a stored row produced them; a sample row wears idle grey, never the green of a real run.
Exactly three identity tints (sage/aqua/mauve), each proven 30 degrees clear of the accent and of every state colour.
DM Sans body, Manrope headings, JetBrains Mono reserved strictly for measurement.
Four fixed columns at wide (68 / 276 / fluid / 320), collapsing through two breakpoints; no section repeats the title of another.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Azure is the only interaction colour. It appears as a fill (with a dark glyph) or as its tint family (wash/line) — nothing else on the bench goes blue to mean clickable.

rules.name: The Dark-Glyph Rule
rules.body: A light accent or identity tint on a dark ground cannot carry white text. Every azure fill and every identity tile takes a dark glyph (--on-azure, or the tint's own dark glyph). identity.test.ts asserts a tile is never given a white glyph.

rules.name: The Stored-Row Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red are only ever produced by a stored row. A seeded sample wears idle grey (raised + ink-2); a fabricated success state is a defect, not a colour.

rules.name: The Three-Mark Rule
rules.body: Identity is exactly three tints (sage/aqua/mauve) — a measured ceiling: with azure owning interaction and green/amber/red owning state, the cool half of the wheel has room for three marks at 30 degrees of separation, so identity is led by the avatar glyph and the tint is secondary. Adding a fourth hue requires changing the accent or the semantics first.

rules.name: The Monospace-Means-Measurement Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono marks only measured data — a count, a time, a token figure, a language tag. It never sets prose.

rules.name: The Naming Rule
rules.body: The section panel is titled by what it holds (Shortcuts, The bench, Reporting lines, Routines, Connectors, Workspace) while the work surface carries the section title. Neither repeats the other.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Elevation is a surface step plus a hairline. --shadow-lift appears only where a layer leaves the grid and floats.

dos: Do carry elevation with a graphite step plus a rule hairline; reserve --shadow-lift for floating layers (dialog, toast, jump, overlay drawers) only.
Do put a dark glyph (--on-azure, or the tint's own dark glyph) on every azure or identity fill.
Do source green/amber/red only from toneOf(status) on a stored row, and render a seeded sample as idle grey.
Do title the section panel by what it holds and the work surface by the section — never both the same word.
Do use JetBrains Mono only for measurement (counts, times, tokens, code, language tags).
Do keep identity to the three tints led by the avatar glyph; keep a tertiary text at ink-3 no lighter than raised (4.5:1).
Do keep every one-off surface hex out of :root until it has a second use.
donts: Don't add a fourth identity hue without first changing the accent or the state semantics — the tests will fail.
Don't promote a single-use surface hex into a token before it has a second use.
Don't reintroduce the deleted Overview devices: the hero illustration, the four large stat cards, per-card ghost numerals, eyebrow/kicker labels above headings, or duplicated Upcoming/Recent panels.
Don't give a light accent or tint fill white text.
Don't use a shadow to make a resting card or button lift — that breaks the flat graphite construction.
Don't use a colour outside azure/state/identity to signal interactivity.
Don't set prose in the monospace face, or place an uppercase kicker above a heading.
notCanonized: The routine dialog's mark references var(--azure-deep), which is not defined in :root; the fill falls back and the mark is otherwise plain azure. Recorded as a defect, not promoted as a token.

The delete-confirmation primary button overrides itself inline to a filled --fault ground with a hard offset shadow (0 1px 2px rgba(155,39,32,.3)). That contradicts both the .danger ghost rule and the flat elevation system, so it is not canonized for future surfaces.
